title: The Indian king who adopted hundreds of Polish children
hook: An Indian king adopted hundreds of Polish children.
summary: In 1942, Maharaja Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar sheltered hundreds of Polish refugee children at Balachadi, and Warsaw later named a square after him.

lines.text: An Indian king adopted hundreds of Polish children.
In nineteen forty-two they were refugees, many without parents.
Then Maharaja Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar offered them a home in India.
At Balachadi he built a camp with food, teachers and play.
He told them they were not orphans anymore. They were his children.
When the war ended, they left to build lives around the world.
Decades later, Warsaw named a square after him: the Good Maharaja.
Remembered in a city he never ruled.

post.caption:
An Indian maharaja gave hundreds of Polish children a safe home in the middle of a war, and Warsaw still honours him.
Would you have known this story?
